trigger_rule: Top-1 in {collie, border_collie} AND pair_mass = p_collie + p_border_collie >= 0.30 AND pair_margin = abs(p_collie - p_border_collie) <= 0.30
probability_source: full 136-dim softmax (never derived from Top-K truncation)
selection_rule_applied: 3) trigger rate <= 50% of the Top-1-in-pair subset
4) among zero-out-of-group combinations take the largest margin tier
selection_note: The plan's step 4 was worded as 'take the largest margin (strictest)', which is directionally wrong: a larger margin threshold is more permissive. Per the stated intent (conservative, hint only when genuinely hard to separate) this step was executed as: among combinations with zero out-of-group false triggers, take the largest margin tier. The correction is recorded here rather than applied silently.
key_finding: Among the 14 images whose true label is collie and whose Top-1 falls in the pair, pair_margin is >= 0.7131 for every one (min 0.7131, max 0.9986): the model is essentially never torn between these two breeds for real collies. The hint therefore fires only when a real border_collie is close to collie.
small_denominator_warning: val has only 16 collie and 15 border_collie images; the Top-1-in-pair subset is only 29; only 3 images trigger. Every ratio here has an extremely small denominator and must not be extrapolated, nor used to claim the hint improves classification accuracy.
mass_non_binding_note: At margin <= 0.30, mass values from 0.10 to 0.50 give identical trigger sets (3 images), i.e. pair_mass is far above every threshold in this subset. 0.30 was chosen for consistency with the existing four-breed mass gate, not because the data favour it.
